messages.subject: effective distance radius with R
parts:
Hi,

 

Using mrds package in R, I wanted to compute EDR value of point transect data.

I used predict function with esw=TRUE but the value obtained is completely unreliable and superior to the right truncation.

 

(for example I obtained the value of  2.77 for a right truncation at 1.8 and distance software gave me something like 0.9 for the same dataset)

 

Is there some kind of adjustments to obtain the true value ? or do I miss something ?

 

Thanks for help.

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] effective distance radius with R
parts:
Dear Thibault,

For point transect data predict() returns the effective area of
detection (usually denoted by the Greek letter nu), equal to pi*w^2*p
see the Introductory book page 54.

It seems that the predict documentation is not correct in this regard. I
will ensure that this documentation is updated for the next release of mrds.

Apologies for the confusion!

best,
--dave
